traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 335 Polemoniaceae: annual to perennial herbs, rarely shrubs; leaves alternate or opposite, entire or palmately or pinnately divided; flowers regular, rarely nearly two-lipped, often crowded in corymbs or heads; sepals 5, joined; corolla of 5 united petals, a tube; stamens 5 on the corolla; ovary superior, of 3 (rarely 2) cells; fruit a capsule, rarely staying shut. The phloxes' salver-shaped corolla is from common knowledge, inferred.
